Expanding TRICARE coverage for military families is long overdue, but let's cut through the bipartisan confetti. The Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act (H.R. 4768) fixes a 14-year-old disparity where military families paid $337-$727/month for coverage civilian plans provided free. Question: Why did Congress wait until 2025 to align TRICARE with ACA standards they imposed on private insurers in 2010?

Real support means funding this $8,724/year savings per family by cutting bureaucratic bloat, not adding to the deficit. The Pentagon just blew $1.7 trillion on F-35s that can't fly in rain - redirect that waste to troops instead of applauding basic fairness as an achievement.
